title: Funny how our idea of success changes with time.
excerpt: There was a time when I dreamed of a PhD abroad, an IIM, prestigious degrees and a career that would make me stand out. I wanted to go places, achieve things and become somebody. I still have those ambitions, but lately, I've been wondering if that's all there is to life. Perhaps I just want enough money, my parents around, time for the things I love, and the freedom to live without constantly chasing the next milestone. I'm so tired of this social media FOMO…
full_text:
Funny how our idea of success changes with time.

There was a time when I dreamed of a PhD abroad, an IIM, prestigious degrees and a career that would make me stand out. I wanted to go places, achieve things and become somebody.

I still have those ambitions, but lately, I've been wondering if that's all there is to life.

Perhaps I just want enough money, my parents around, time for the things I love, and the freedom to live without constantly chasing the next milestone. I'm so tired of this social media FOMO…

title: Turiya
excerpt: Came to know about this in a lecture by Swami Sarvapriyananda. Beyond waking, dreaming and deep sleep lies what the Mandukya Upanishad calls the Fourth: Turiya. Not another state of consciousness, but the underlying reality in which all three states appear. It asks what remains when every experience disappears?
full_text:
Turiya

Came to know about this in a lecture by Swami Sarvapriyananda.

Beyond waking, dreaming and deep sleep lies what the Mandukya Upanishad calls the Fourth: Turiya.

Not another state of consciousness, but the underlying reality in which all three states appear.

It asks what remains when every experience disappears?

title: Your thoughts change your feelings change.
excerpt: Even your sense of who you are changes over time.But you are aware of these changes. Advaita Vedānta asks: what is this awareness that notices it all? Instead of asking what you are thinking, ask yourself: Who is aware of the thought?
full_text:
Your thoughts change your feelings change. Even your sense of who you are changes over time.But you are aware of these changes.

Advaita Vedānta asks: what is this awareness that notices it all?

Instead of asking what you are thinking, ask yourself: Who is aware of the thought?

title: The more I read about Atman, the more I wonder: what do I really mean when I say "I"?
excerpt: My body changes. My thoughts change. Even my idea of myself changes. So what is this "I" that stays through all of it?
full_text:
The more I read about Atman, the more I wonder: what do I really mean when I say "I"?

My body changes. My thoughts change. Even my idea of myself changes.

So what is this "I" that stays through all of it?

title: "God is dead. God remains dead. And we have killed him." - Friedrich Nietzsche
excerpt: Nietzsche's real question wasn't about God. It was: if nobody hands you meaning anymore, do you actually have the courage to build your own or do you just grab the nearest replacement dogma and pretend that was your choice all along? That's a harder question than it sounds.
full_text:
"God is dead. God remains dead. And we have killed him."

- Friedrich Nietzsche

Nietzsche's real question wasn't about God. It was: if nobody hands you meaning anymore, do you actually have the courage to build your own or do you just grab the nearest replacement dogma and pretend that was your choice all along?

That's a harder question than it sounds.
